attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: Keeps 'virtually none', 'yet' and the named researchers. A firm present-state observation as of May 2022.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. It uses the context's examples (comprehension, intent, reasoning, compositionality) as guides, and 'solved' means reliable competence. The problem inventory is unspecified, so the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed survey from April 2022 urging caution about benchmark success. It does not list or count the problems Marcus refers to.
Gato report from May 2022 claims promise in out-of-distribution learning. Promise is not a solution, and it covers only part of the problem set.

reviews.rationale: The packet sets out no inventory of the referenced problems and no assessment of how many were solved by May 2022. e1 and e2 are relevant context but settle neither the support nor the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: 'I don't think' states a firm opinion, not a graded hedge. The proposition is phrased as Marcus's belief, but what can be tested is the capability comparison with Flash Fill, which the contract scores.

contract.note: Reading 'can match' as systems existing in May 2022 fits the present tense, and the one-example criterion comes from his 'one-trial' description. Choices about 'pure' and the meaning of 'match' are the evaluator's, so they decide the result.

evidence.note: RobustFill (2017) comparison used four examples, not one, and predates the target window.
The synthesis model matching Flash Fill relies on deterministic, non-neural execution, so it is arguably not 'pure'. It is also a four-example setup. It neither supports nor contradicts.

reviews.rationale: No matched one-example comparison of pure neural systems available in May 2022 against Flash Fill is in the packet. The nearest evidence changes the example count and adds symbolic execution, so it cannot settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'current', 'remotely close', 'arbitrary', speaker intent and coherent reasoning. Saying 'not close to A or B' is equivalent to his 'not close to A, nor to B'.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: 'arbitrary' means diverse unseen inputs, not perfection, and 'not remotely close' is treated as stronger than 'unsolved'. 'Remotely close' has no threshold, so interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: The Gato paper calls its own dialogue rudimentary. That limits one model only, not all contemporary AI.
Google's own PaLM blog post (a company disclosure) reports strong results on selected benchmarks. It does not show reliable comprehension of arbitrary text, speaker intent or general reasoning.

reviews.rationale: Neither item is a broad evaluation of leading May 2022 systems against the described competence. Gato's limits do not cover all AI, and PaLM's benchmark gains do not show near-reliable arbitrary comprehension. The evidence does not settle 'remotely close'.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: Faithfully restates the compound claim: billions spent, data growth from MB to GB, parameters from millions to trillions, and errors that persist.

contract.note: Requiring evidence for each component is fair, and missing expense records explicitly do not count as contradiction. How 'poured into' and 'discomprehending errors' are read decides the result.

evidence.note: The Switch Transformer paper (Jan 2021) reports 1.6T total parameters, supporting the trillions endpoint only.
The Pile (Dec 2020) is an 825 GiB corpus, supporting the gigabytes endpoint. It does not show the megabyte starting point.
February 2022 study finds Transformer seq2seq models still fail at structural generalization. This partly supports 'remain', but not continuity since 1988.

reviews.rationale: The scale endpoints and contemporary compositional failures are supported, and nothing contradicts any component. But the multibillion Transformer spending, the megabyte starting point and continuity of errors since 1988 are unestablished. The compound claim cannot be settled.
